worked_solution:
We differentiate each component separately.

- For the $x$-component $x(t)={e}^{2t}(t+1),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t) & =(2{e}^{2t})(t+1)+{e}^{2t}(1) \\  & =2{e}^{2t}(t+1)+{e}^{2t},\end{aligned}
$$

and therefore,

$$
{x}^{′}(0)=2{e}^{2\cdot 0}(0+1)+{e}^{2\cdot 0}=3.
$$

- For the $y$-component $y(t)=\sqrt{9-{t}^{2}},$ we have

$$
{y}^{′}(t)=-\frac{t}{\sqrt{9-{t}^{2}}},
$$

and therefore,

$$
{y}^{′}(0)=-\frac{0}{\sqrt{9-{0}^{2}}}=0.
$$

So, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(0) & =⟨{x}^{′}(0),\,{y}^{′}(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨3,\,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
